unit.why: A narrative, quoted from the son's manuscript, about the death of R. Alexander Sender of Komarno. It reports his death in a mystical unification of self-sacrifice, a dream testimony, a pillar of fire over his grave, and his corpse trembling when a tzaddik asked him to pray.

stories.start_quote: עו״ש בכתב יד הנזכר לעיל. אבי נשמתו עדן
stories.end_quote: שכן הי׳ דרכו באימה ופחד עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: The son recounts that his father, of the soul-root of Maimonides, died in a mystical unification of self-sacrifice like the Ten Martyrs, as R. Jacob Isaac of Lublin confirmed in a dream; a pillar of fire was seen over his grave, and his body on the bier trembled twice when the Rabbi of Ohel asked him to pray against a decree.

tags.why: The whole story centres on the tzaddik's death and its aftermath.

quotes: ונפטר ביחוד של מסירת נפש של ר"ע
כמו עשרה הרוגי מלכות ביחוד נפלא ובמס״נ
tags.why: He died while performing a mystical unification.
The yihud is contemplative mystical practice.

quotes: שאמר לו רבינו מוהרי"י מלובלין בחלום
tags.why: The Seer of Lublin reveals the manner of the death in a dream.

quotes: שאמר לו רבינו מוהרי"י מלובלין בחלום
אמר לו הצדיק הרב מאוהעל שיתפלל
tags.why: A dead tzaddik speaks in a dream, and the dead man is addressed and responds.

quotes: ועמוד של אש נראה על קברו
tags.why: A pillar of fire over his grave is a sign of his righteousness.
The corpse trembles as though alive.
His habit was to pray in awe and fear.
